summary.en: Partly delivered: the Tools page has an Authenticator section with My accounts and App locks. My accounts is a general authenticator: it adds accounts from an otpauth link (parameters honoured) or by hand, shows each account's code grouped for reading with a seconds countdown and the next code, copies a code, renames, reorders and deletes with confirmation, searches, protects the whole list for the Windows account with DPAPI, and exports or imports an AES-256-GCM backup under a passphrase. App locks pairs an authenticator app with a lock (QR code, Base32 text, a code typed back) and runs the RFC 6238 vectors. Link parsing, codes against the RFC 6238 vectors, the vault and backup are covered by UI-state checks. Registration from a QR image file or the clipboard (decoded in-process with ZXing.Net, through the same link parser; round trip checked in code) is built but has not been driven in the built window. Camera registration, grouping, a clock-skew warning and a super-confirmed secrets export are not built, and nothing has been driven in the built window.

summary.en: An installed copy checks the public RELEASES file in the background (once per launch, after a short delay), compares versions with framework-free logic, runs Update.exe to stage a newer full package and shows a non-blocking banner naming the build as unsigned. summary.en: Partly delivered: every settings row that holds a value has a lock button, and every button, switch, option, drop-down, text field and slider on every page has Lock this control on its right-click menu, with a stable id (its automation id, otherwise its page, kind, English name and position among identical elements). Each lock chooses one of eight policies: confirm only, PIN, password, authenticator app, PIN plus password, password plus authenticator, PIN plus authenticator, or password plus PIN plus authenticator. PINs and passwords are stored as salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashes, the authenticator secret is protected with Windows DPAPI, attempts are backoff-limited and persist, and single-use recovery codes are made at setup. Each lock also chooses how long an unlock lasts (this action only, 5 minutes, 1 hour, or until the app closes) and closes again by itself, including at the next launch. Settings has a Locks manager listing every lock with search, filters, export, unlock, lock again, change policy and single or bulk removal. A locked control is disabled, locks persist and are recorded in history without credentials, and import, reset, palette controls and the accessibility menu respect them. The logic is covered by focused checks that were seen failing first. Tabs and tab groups (the pinned region, the open region and the navigation rail) can be locked from their context menus and refuse switching, closing, moving and pinning; every appearance value, each colour role, saved presets and each property of a customized element has its own lock that holds against editing, presets, paste, undo, import and reset; clicking a locked control opens its unlock prompt instead of doing nothing; locked tabs and commands are labelled in the palette, the tab search and the New tab catalog (with an optional setting to hide them, announced in each list); locked tabs are kept out of bulk closes; and the unlock prompt has a PIN keypad that shares the one validator and attempt budget with typing. These rules are covered by focused checks that were seen failing first. Not built: user-made tab groups, a tab-group search and an all-windows tab search, a keypad in the PIN wizard, and an unlock prompt anchored beside the control (it is the shared overlay dialog). Nothing has been driven in the built window.

summary.en: Partly delivered: a Support Tickets desk reachable from the unlock prompt (Forgotten your password?), the lock wizard and the Locks manager, the Tools page and the command palette. A ticket has a category, a severity that is recorded and then treated like every other, a description, a locally generated number such as TKT-20261104-0001 and a status that advances by itself or on request (new, acknowledged, investigating, resolved) with canned replies. The resolution only opens the application-data folder in the file manager and shows its exact path with a copy button; the app never deletes it. One plain line, unaffected by the funny level, says nothing is sent anywhere and nobody is reading. Tickets are stored locally, searchable with the regex-wired search, exportable and removable in bulk. The logic and the absence of network or delete code are covered by checks that were seen failing first. Nothing has been driven in the built window, so the folder opening and the layout at narrow widths are unverified.

summary.en: Partly delivered: unlocking climbs confirm, then each credential of the lock's policy in a fixed order (PIN, password, authenticator code) shown as Step n of m, then a persistent exponential wait (free tries, then 30 seconds doubling to one hour) with an honest live countdown. A wrong answer at any step counts once against one shared budget and restarts the attempt at the first factor. A single-use recovery code is reachable at any time, the data-folder recovery route and a Forgotten your password link to the local Support Tickets desk sit beside the prompt, and waiting alone never unlocks anything. While waiting, a person can play a dish question (a picture from the public catalogue, or a name question when offline), ten sums and whack-a-mole to end the wait early. Questions are made and graded in framework-free code against single-use nonces, a rolling budget of three wins an hour caps it, an early or replayed answer is refused, and a win clears only the wait: it signs nobody in, refunds no attempt and does not slow the escalation. School mode starts at the sums. Grading runs in the same process as the views. These rules are checked in code; nothing has been driven in the built window.
